column1: # Debris the OCR pulled into an entry, and the repair for it.
# This is the third repair layer, and it exists because the other two do not
# fit what is wrong here:
#   corrections.tsv  substitutes whole words, everywhere they occur. Most of
#                    the damage below is punctuation, a footnote marker or a
#                    page's running head, none of which is a word.
#   proofed.tsv      replaces an entry with a fresh transcription. Retyping a
#                    600-character entry to delete one asterisk introduces more
#                    risk than it removes.
# So a repair here is a single anchored edit: `find` must occur in the entry
# **exactly once**. qa.py refuses to apply it otherwise — 0 matches means the
# line is stale and is reported like a redundant recovered.tsv line, more than
# one means the edit is ambiguous and would be a guess. That is what stops a
# repair from quietly landing in the wrong place after the parser changes.
# Every line was checked against the page image, which is why the page is
# recorded. The scan page is the PDF page; the book's printed folio runs three
# behind it. Two OCR passes agreeing was NOT taken as sufficient — see saying
# 171, where they agree and the page still does not settle it.
# Format: number<TAB>find<TAB>replace<TAB>scan page<TAB>note
# An empty `replace` deletes.
# --- the next saying bled in, and its number was destroyed --------------
# The same defect as trap 4 in CLAUDE.md, twice. Both of the swallowed sayings
# were already recovered into recovered.tsv, so the corpus looked complete
# while the duplicate went on being printed under the wrong number.
